name: kql-dangling-ids
description: A dangling {id:} / (id:) matcher fails the query only in the mandatory pattern. Inside OPTIONAL it degrades to 'no optional match', inside NOT the clause simply excludes nothing, and inside a UNION branch that branch contributes the empty set.
setup: UPSERT { CONCEPT ?t { {type: "$ConceptType", name: "PairNode"} } CONCEPT ?p1 { {type: "$PropositionType", name: "p1"} } CONCEPT ?p2 { {type: "$PropositionType", name: "p2"} } CONCEPT ?a1 { {type: "PairNode", name: "A1"} } CONCEPT ?a2 { {type: "PairNode", name: "A2"} } CONCEPT ?b1 { {type: "PairNode", name: "B1"} } CONCEPT ?b2 { {type: "PairNode", name: "B2"} } PROPOSITION ?l1 { (?a1, "p1", ?b1) } PROPOSITION ?l2 { (?a2, "p1", ?b2) } PROPOSITION ?l3 { (?a1, "p2", ?b2) } PROPOSITION ?l4 { (?a2, "p2", ?b2) } }

cases.name: a dangling id in the mandatory pattern reports not found
a dangling id inside OPTIONAL keeps the outer solution
the unmatched OPTIONAL variable projects null
a dangling id inside NOT makes the clause exclude nothing
the same NOT with a resolvable target still excludes
a dangling concept id in a UNION branch contributes the empty set
a dangling link id in a UNION branch contributes the empty set
